name: Portal Outage Escalation (911)
trigger: You notice, or a customer reports, that the Portal is down or broken.
purpose: If the Portal is mildly broken for customers, or completely broken for Build staff, and nobody pages engineering, customers sit in a broken product until morning. This gets an on-call engineer on it immediately. Company-wide, all markets.
doneWhen: The issue is resolved, or #general has an outage description and an expected ETA (or an explicit "no ETA") on resolution.
timeToRun: 5 minutes to escalate, then until resolution or handoff

steps.title: Decide if it's a 911
steps.trigger: You notice, or a customer reports, that the Portal is down or broken.
steps.work: Check one thing: are customers hitting a real problem? Super long load times, tickets not updating, error messages, or the site is down. A Portal that functions but is merely slow is not a 911. Never send bugs, tolerable slowness, or anything that can wait until morning to 911@; 911 pages a human engineer.
rules: Never send bugs, tolerable slowness, or anything that can wait until morning to 911@.

steps.title: Post it in #product-eng instead
steps.trigger: The Portal is functioning, just slow or mildly buggy.
steps.work: Post the problem in #product-eng. You're done; no page goes out.

steps.title: Ask Brent whether it's a 911
steps.trigger: You can't tell whether the problem clears the 911 bar.
steps.work: Send Brent what's broken, what you were doing, and roughly when it started. He makes the call.

steps.title: Email 911@getthom.com
steps.work: Email 911@getthom.com with what's broken, what you were doing, and roughly when it started. Don't worry about formatting it nicely. This calls an on-call engineer for immediate attention.

steps.title: Stay on it until resolved or handed off
steps.work: Stay in contact with the on-call engineer and get an ETA. If you 911'd something that turns out to be minor, tell the engineer and move it to #product-eng; no harm done. If the on-call engineer never responds, the source page leaves the fallback TBD for the owner to fill in.
steps.doneWhen: You have an ETA, or the issue is resolved.

steps.title: Does #general need an outage post?
steps.trigger: You have an ETA from the on-call engineer, or you're signing off.
steps.work: Post in #general with the outage description and the ETA if either is true: the engineer says the fix will take more than 2 hours, or you're signing off before it's resolved and there's no ETA (say so in the post). If the issue resolves quickly, no post is needed.

steps.title: Post the outage description and ETA in #general
steps.trigger: The fix will take over 2 hours, or you're signing off unresolved.
steps.work: Post the outage description and the ETA in #general. If there is no ETA and you're signing off, say "no ETA, signing off" explicitly.
